en: Oṃ, homage to all buddhas and bodhisattvas!

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain, in the great shrine formerly inhabited by the Conquerors, upon the circle of the earth empowered by the Tathāgata’s blessing, on the Dharma-throne praised by Bodhisattvas, in that region of the earth venerated by gods, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas, which incites roots of virtue, which is the source of the Tathāgata, the expression of the gateways of Dharma, and the source of the Bodhisattvas.

O you who have arisen from immeasurable virtues, within the range of the Tathāgatas; the Blessed One who has perfectly awakened to the equality of all phenomena, who has well set in motion the wheel of Dharma, who has well disciplined an infinite host of disciples, who has attained mastery over all phenomena, who thoroughly knows the methods for the inclinations of all beings, who has reached the supreme perfection of the faculties, who is skilled in uprooting the latent tendencies and the connections between the continuities of all beings, and whose effortless Buddha-activity is never-ceasing—[he was] together with a great community of monks.

Together with six hundred thousand bhikṣus—all of whom were well-bred, whose minds were perfectly liberated through right knowledge, who had eradicated the continuity of all afflictions and their latent tendencies, who were sons of the Tathāgata, the King of Dharma, skilled in dwelling in the profound Dharma, emerged from the dharma of non-apprehension, endowed with graceful deportment, become great objects of veneration, and who had correctly practiced the command of the Tathāgata—as well as with an immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas who had emerged into omniscience that ranges without attachment.

by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, who were illuminated by the knowledge and liberation of the insight of the Dharma-clouds of great loving-kindness and great compassion; who satisfy the entire world by raining down the water of nectar like clouds; whose minds are equal to the earth that supports all beings; who are free from attachment and aversion; and who cause the harvest of the various factors conducive to enlightenment to flourish.

They were those who, by emitting rays of wisdom exceeding the solar orb, dispelled the darkness of delusion and attained the illumination of the path; they were skilled in awakening the lotuses of sentient beings, ripening their roots of virtue, drying up the waters of craving, establishing the activities of knowledge, and wandering upon the path of the grove of great supernormal powers; like the moon, they possessed minds equal toward all the world, satisfying and gladdening their intentions through skillful means that demonstrated neither decrease nor increase.

They were firmly established in the four divine abodes with a resolve as steadfast as Mount Sumeru; their four sides were the four jewels, unshakable by the winds of any sensory realm; they had risen above worldly dharmas and reached the illumination that reveals all buddha-fields; they were like the great ocean, filled with the waters of the Dharma in vast vessels of dhāraṇīs and mindfulness, containing the jewels of the bodhisattva’s conduct upon which the entire world depends for its livelihood.

They were like lions, with tails of loving-kindness increased by their practice of truthful conduct, eyes of calm abiding and insight, and who, through not being terrified of the profound Dharma, destroyed all rival disputants; they were endowed with all virtues, never ceasing their engagement in the bodhisattva practices throughout limitless hundreds of thousands of incalculable eons, and had reached no end nor final consummation.

They were as follows: the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Samantāvabhāsānāvaraṇadarśin; the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Sarvakṣetrālaṃkāravyūhasaṃdarśaka; the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Tathāgatagotrasambhavācāramati; and the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Sarveryāpathavinītāvikopanasaṃdarśaka.

and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Anantapratibhānaketudhvajavikurvitaghoṣa; and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Śubhakanakanicitaprabhātejoraśmi; and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Prajñāviniścayapadapratibhāna; and with the bodhisattva mahāsattva named Aparimitapuṇyajñānasaṃbhāropastambhopacita—along with these and other immeasurable bodhisattva mahāsattvas, headed by such as these.

There, indeed, the Blessed One was proclaiming the Dharma discourse titled "The Unobstructed Gateway to the Setting Forth and Departure in the Bodhisattva Practice. Then, perceiving that sixteen years had passed since his full enlightenment, and recognizing the widespread propagation of the holy life by the Blessed One, and seeing that great assembly of bodhisattvas, he understood: "Truly, these bodhisattvas who have gathered here are the upholders of the Tathāgata’s treasury of Dharma. Having understood this, it occurred to him: "What if I were now to provide even greater support for the bodhisattvas?"

"I shall fully proclaim the Dharma discourse titled 'The Unobstructed Gateway of Setting Out and Departing upon the Bodhisattva Course,' by means of the great miraculous manifestation of a Tathāgata and the great supernatural power of a Tathāgata; that is to say, for the purpose of causing the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas, to enter the domain of the Tathāgata.
Then, at that time, the Blessed One entered the Tathāgata-samādhi called "The Manifestation of the Domain of the Buddha as it Truly Is."
